title: Location pings drown the trip database
description: Five million online drivers ping every four seconds, creating about 1.25 million location writes/s. Each ping replaces the last position, but accepted trips must survive crashes. Which storage split matches those different needs?

options.text: Put both current positions and accepted trips in one non-replicated in-memory map.
options.explanation: Positions can recover from the next ping, but losing accepted trip state violates the durability requirement.

options.text: Write every position synchronously into the main trip transaction before acknowledging the ping.
options.explanation: This spends transactional durability on rapidly obsolete data and makes location volume compete with financially important trip state.

options.text: Index drivers only by driver ID in a durable log and scan it for every nearby-driver query.
options.explanation: A driver-ID log does not provide efficient proximity lookup. Scanning positions on every request ignores the spatial access pattern.

options.text: Keep latest positions in a replicated, expiring geo index partitioned by city, and accepted trip state in a durable database.
options.explanation: The geo index serves nearby-driver queries and can refill after loss from fresh pings. Durable trip transitions remain separate; sampled trip locations for disputes can use another durable path.
